facts.label: Descrever uma pessoa
facts.sub: Use She's + adjetivo (tall, shy) e She has + cabelo/olhos: She has long, dark hair.

facts.label: Seja gentil
facts.sub: Prefira palavras neutras ou positivas, como tall, friendly, kind. Evite comentar peso, idade e aparência de estranhos, pois pode ser considerado rude. Sobre pessoas que você não conhece, “Not sure” é uma boa resposta.

facts.label: Achar alguém
facts.sub: Para encontrar uma pessoa num lugar cheio, diga o que você veste ou onde está: “I’m wearing a red jacket” ou “I’m near the entrance”. Roupas e cores ajudam mais do que traços físicos.

compare.br: In Brazil people often make friendly comments about looks, like hair or style, and use affectionate nicknames.
compare.us: In the USA people also compliment hair or clothes, but they avoid comments about age, weight or skin with strangers.
compare.tip: Compliment what a person chooses, like clothes or style: “I like your jacket!”

pages.title: My sister Ana and a girl with red hair · 1/3
paragraphs: My name is Sofia, and I live in **Tampa**. Yesterday I was at a park with my sister, Ana. A man named Cole saw us. He asked, “Who is that woman?” “That’s my sister,” I said. “**Do you know him**?” Ana asked me. “Not yet,” I said, “but he looks nice.”

Cole said, “She’s tall. Is she shy?” “No, she’s very friendly,” I said. “**What does she look like**?” he asked. “She has long, dark hair,” I said. “She’s tall, and she has brown eyes.” Cole smiled. “**That’s him**!” Ana said, when she saw her friend Tom with a big dog.

pages.title: My sister Ana and a girl with red hair · 2/3
paragraphs: I love to describe people. It reminds me of a book, “Anne of Green Gables.” L. M. Montgomery, a Canadian writer, wrote it in 1908. Anne is an orphan girl with red hair and a big imagination. She goes to live on a farm in Canada and talks a lot. Everyone remembers her red hair.

Describing people is fun, but be careful. Say nice things like “She’s friendly” or “He’s tall.” Do not talk about weight or age with strangers. And if you do not know a person well, you can say, “**Not sure**.”

pages.focus: pausa e ritmo com a vírgula (“long, dark hair”)
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em listas de adjetivos e em frases longas, a vírgula pede uma pequena pausa e uma entonação que não desce por completo. Sem isso, a descrição vira um bloco só. Ajuda o ouvinte a entender cada traço.
pages.how: Em “She has long, dark hair”, diga LONG, faça uma pausa curtinha, mantenha a voz no meio e diga DARK HAIR, descendo no fim. A pausa é rápida, só um respiro.
pages.tip: Conte nos dedos cada característica: um dedo para long, outro para dark. Faça a pausa quando trocar de dedo.
